sentences.zh: 曹志

translations.literal: Cao Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi

sentences.zh: 曹志，字允恭，譙國譙人，魏陳思王植之孽子也。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi, courtesy name Yonggong, was a man of Qiao in the Princedom of Qiao, a secondary son by a concubine of Cao Zhi, Prince of Chensi of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi, style Yonggong, came from Qiao in the kingdom of Qiao. He was a younger son born to a concubine of Wei’s Prince of Chensi, the celebrated poet whose personal name was homophonous with his son’s but written with a different graph.

sentences.zh: 少好學，以才行稱，夷簡有大度，兼善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, was praised for talent and conduct, was easygoing and simple and had great breadth of mind, and was also skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved study and was esteemed for ability and character: open, unpretentious, and large-minded, and a capable horseman and archer as well.

sentences.zh: 植曰：「此保家主也。

translations.literal: The prince said, “This one is a master who will preserve the family.”
translations.idiomatic: His father the prince said, “This is the son who will keep our house secure.”

sentences.zh: 」立以為嗣。

translations.literal: ” He established him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was named heir.

sentences.zh: 後改封濟北王。

translations.literal: Later his fief was changed and he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to the title of Prince of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 武帝為撫軍將軍，迎陳留王於鄴，志夜謁見，帝與語，自暮達旦，甚奇之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was General Who Pacifies the Army and welcomed the Prince of Chenliu at Ye, Zhi went by night to have audience; the emperor conversed with him from dusk until dawn and greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Wu still held the post of General Who Pacifies the Army and had gone to Ye to welcome the Prince of Chenliu, Cao Zhi sought a night audience. They talked from evening until dawn, and the future emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，降為鄄城縣公。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the abdication, he was demoted to Duke of Juancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: After the abdication he was reduced in rank to Duke of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔在前世，雖曆運迭興，至於先代苗裔，傳祚不替，或列籓九服，式序王官。

translations.literal: An edict said, “In former ages, although the cyclical fortune rose in turn, as for the descendants of prior dynasties, their transmission of the mandate was not cut off; some were arrayed as feudatories throughout the nine domains, or were ordered in sequence among the king’s offices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: “Under earlier dynasties, even as Heaven’s mandate shifted from house to house, scions of fallen lines often kept their titles, whether as feudal lords across the realm or as officers in the royal administration.”

sentences.zh: 選眾命賢，惟德是與，蓋至公之道也。

translations.literal: Choosing from the multitude and appointing the worthy, giving place only to virtue—this is the way of utmost impartiality.”
translations.idiomatic: To elevate the worthy from among the many and bind oneself to nothing but merit is the path of perfect fairness.”

sentences.zh: 魏氏諸王公養德藏器，壅滯曠久，前雖有詔，當須簡授，而自頃眾職少缺，未得式敘。

translations.literal: The various princes and dukes of the Wei house have nurtured virtue and hidden their talents, blocked and stagnant for a long time; although there was previously an edict that they should await selection and appointment, yet recently many posts have had few incumbents, and they have not been able to be ordered in due sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s imperial clansmen have long kept their abilities in reserve while appointments were blocked. Earlier orders called for careful selection, yet many offices still stand thinly staffed, and proper order in ennoblement has not been achieved.

sentences.zh: 前濟北王曹志履德清純，才高行潔，好古博物，為魏宗英，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The former Prince of Jibei, Cao Zhi, treads virtue in purity and clarity, talent is high and conduct is clean, he loves antiquity and broadly knows things, and is an outstanding one among the Wei imperial clan; We greatly praise him.
translations.idiomatic: The former Prince of Jibei, Cao Zhi, walks a path of unstained integrity, combines high talent with spotless conduct, and cherishes the classical tradition—an ornament of the Wei bloodline whom I hold in high regard.

sentences.zh: 其以志為樂平太守。

translations.literal: Let Zhi be made Administrator of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Let Cao Zhi be appointed Administrator of Leping.”

sentences.zh: 」志在郡上書，以為宜尊儒重道，請為博士置吏卒。

translations.literal: ” When Zhi was in the commandery he submitted a memorial, holding that one should honor Confucians and esteem the Way, and requested that for the erudits clerks and soldiers be assigned.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the commandery he petitioned the throne to exalt Confucian learning and the Way, and asked that the court assign attendants to the academicians.”

sentences.zh: 遷章武、趙郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Administrator of Zhangwu and Zhao commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to Administrator of Zhangwu and of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 雖累郡職，不以政事為意，晝則遊獵，夜誦《詩》《書》，以聲色自娛，當時見者未能審其量也。

translations.literal: Although he repeatedly held commandery posts, he did not take administrative affairs to heart; by day he roamed and hunted, by night he recited the Odes and the Documents, and amused himself with music and women; those who saw him at the time could not yet fathom his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served several terms as a commandery governor, he showed little interest in routine administration: days in the hunt, evenings with the *Classic of Poetry* and the *Book of Documents*, and his own pleasures in music and company—so contemporaries mistook him for a man of no depth.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，詔曰：「鄄城公曹志，篤行履素，達學通識，宜在儒林，以弘胄子之教。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianning era, an edict said, “Duke of Juancheng Cao Zhi, in conduct is earnest and treads simplicity, in learning is comprehensive and in knowledge is penetrating; he should be in the Forest of Scholars, in order to enlarge the instruction of the scions.”
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianning era (275–280) an edict read: “Duke of Juancheng Cao Zhi lives plainly and studies widely; he belongs among Confucian scholars to broaden the education of the heir-apparent’s companions.”

sentences.zh: 其以志為散騎常侍、國子博士。

translations.literal: Let Zhi be made Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and Erudit of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary and Erudit of the National University.”

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗閱《六代論》，問志曰：「是卿先王所作邪？

translations.literal: ” The emperor once perused the “Treatise on the Six Dynasties” and asked Zhi, “Was this composed by your former prince?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once read the *Treatise on the Six Dynasties* and asked Cao Zhi, “Did your royal father write this?”

sentences.zh: 」志對曰：「先王有手所作目錄，請歸尋按。

translations.literal: ” Zhi replied, “The former prince had a catalogue written in his own hand; I beg to return and search according to it.”
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi answered, “My father kept a handwritten catalogue of his works. Allow me to go home and check it.”

sentences.zh: 」還奏曰：「按錄無此。

translations.literal: ” Returning, he reported, “According to the catalogue, this is not there.”
translations.idiomatic: He returned and reported, “That piece is not listed among his papers.”

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誰作？

translations.literal: ” The emperor said, “Who composed it?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, “Then who wrote it?”

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「以臣所聞，是臣族父冏所作。

translations.literal: ” Zhi said, “According to what your subject has heard, it was composed by your subject’s clansman-uncle Jiong.”
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi said, “From what I have learned, it was the work of my kinsman Cao Jiong.”

sentences.zh: 以先王文高名著，欲令書傳於後，是以假託。

translations.literal: Because the former prince’s writing was lofty and his name illustrious, he wished to make the work transmitted to later ages, and therefore falsely attributed it.
translations.idiomatic: Because my father’s literary fame stood so high, Cao Jiong attached the essay to his name so that it might survive.”

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「古來亦多有是。

translations.literal: ” The emperor said, “Since antiquity there have also been many cases of this.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, “Such pious forgeries are nothing new in history.”

sentences.zh: 」顧謂公卿曰：「父子證明，足以為審。

translations.literal: ” Turning, he said to the dukes and ministers, “Father and son have verified and clarified; it is sufficient to be considered settled.”
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the high ministers he added, “When father and son agree like this, the matter is settled.”

sentences.zh: 自今已後，可無復疑。」

translations.literal: From now onward, there need be no further doubt.”
translations.idiomatic: Let no one doubt it again.”

sentences.zh: 後遷祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Libationer of the National University.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸將之國，下太常議崇錫文物。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi, You, was about to go to his state; he sent down to the Minister of Ceremonies for deliberation the enhancing and bestowing of ritual regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima You of Qi was ordered to his fief, the court instructed the Ministry of Ceremonies to debate what honors and ritual gear should attend his departure.

sentences.zh: 時博士秦秀等以為齊王宜內匡朝政，不可之籓。

translations.literal: At that time Erudit Qin Xiu and others held that the Prince of Qi should inwardly assist court governance and could not go to a feudatory.
translations.idiomatic: Erudits such as Qin Xiu argued that the prince ought to remain at court to steady the government rather than leave for his appanage.

sentences.zh: 志又常恨其父不得志于魏，因愴然歎曰：「安有如此之才，如此之親，不得樹本助化，而遠出海隅？

translations.literal: Zhi also constantly resented that his father had not realized his ambitions in Wei; therefore sorrowfully he sighed, saying, “How can there be such talent, such closeness of kinship, yet not be able to plant roots and assist transformation, but instead go far off to the corner of the sea?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi still brooded over how his father had never won his way under Wei. He once said in anguish, “How could a man of such gifts and such nearness to the throne be denied a role at the heart of government, and instead be packed off to the empire’s edge?”

sentences.zh: 晉朝之隆，其殆乎哉！

translations.literal: The flourishing of the Jin court—is it perhaps in peril!”
translations.idiomatic: If that is how Jin treats its own, what hope is there for the dynasty’s greatness!”

sentences.zh: 」乃奏議曰：「伏聞大司馬齊王當出籓東夏，備物盡禮，同之二伯。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he submitted a memorial stating, “Your subject has heard that the Grand Marshal, Prince of Qi, is to go out to his feudatory in eastern summer; full things and complete rites, the same as the two earls.”
translations.idiomatic: He therefore drafted a memorial: “I learn that the Grand Marshal, Prince of Qi, is to take up his fief in the east with every ceremonial honor, as though he were one of the ancient ‘two elders’ who aided the Son of Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 今陛下為聖君，稷、契為賢臣，內有魯、衛之親，外有齊、晉之輔，坐而守安，此萬世之基也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is a sage lord, Ji and Xie are worthy ministers; within there is the closeness of Lu and Wei, without there is the assistance of Qi and Jin; sitting and guarding peace—this is the foundation for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a sage ruler served by men worthy to be called Ji and Xie; within the palace you have the bone-ties of Lu and Wei, beyond it ministers strong as Qi and Jin once were. Peace kept from the capital is a foundation meant to last ages.”

sentences.zh: 古之夾輔王室，同姓則周公其人也，異姓則太公其人也，皆身在內，五世反葬。

translations.literal: Of those who in antiquity flanked and aided the royal house, of the same surname then the Duke of Zhou was such a man; of a different surname then the Grand Duke was such a man; all were personally within, and for five generations returned to be buried.
translations.idiomatic: Those who steadied the Zhou house—the Duke of Zhou among kin, the Grand Duke of Qi among outsiders—stayed at court, and even after five generations their bones came home to the royal domain for burial.”

sentences.zh: 後雖有五霸代興，桓、文譎主，下有請隧之僭，上有九錫之禮，終於譎而不正，驗於尾大不掉，豈與召公之歌《棠棣》，周詩之詠《鴟鴞》同日論哉！

translations.literal: Later although the five hegemons arose in turn, Huan and Wen were deceitful lords; below there was the usurpation of requesting a tunnel, above there was the rite of the nine bestowals; in the end they were deceitful and not correct, verified in the tail being large and not drooping—how can this be discussed on the same day as the Duke of Shao’s song ‘Tangdi,’ or the Zhou poem’s chant ‘Owl’!”
translations.idiomatic: Later ages produced the Five Hegemons: rulers like Duke Huan and Duke Wen who ruled by guile, vassals who dared ask for royal funeral rites, and courts that piled the nine insignia on a subject—power that grew too heavy to control. That world has nothing in common with the Duke of Shao’s hymn to brotherhood in the *Book of Odes*, or with the poem that warns a young king to mind his kin.”

sentences.zh: 今聖朝創業之始，始之不諒，後事難工。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of the founding of the sage court, if the beginning is not trustworthy, later affairs will be hard to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of a dynasty, what is done amiss at the outset cannot easily be set right afterward.”

sentences.zh: 幹植不強，枝葉不茂；

translations.literal: If the trunk is not strong, branches and leaves are not luxuriant;
translations.idiomatic: A weak trunk cannot bear lush branches.”

sentences.zh: 骨骾不存，皮膚不充。

translations.literal: If the bones and frame do not remain, skin and flesh are not filled out.
translations.idiomatic: Strip the bone from the body and the skin has nothing to cling to.”

sentences.zh: 自羲皇以來，豈是一姓之獨有！

translations.literal: Since Fuxi the August, how could it be that one surname alone possesses it!”
translations.idiomatic: Since high antiquity no single lineage has monopolized Heaven’s favor forever.”

sentences.zh: 欲結其心者，當有磐石之固。

translations.literal: Those who wish to bind their hearts ought to have the firmness of a great rock.
translations.idiomatic: If you would win men’s loyalty, your foundations must be rock-solid.”

sentences.zh: 夫欲享萬世之利者，當與天下議之。

translations.literal: Now those who wish to enjoy the benefit of ten thousand generations ought to deliberate with all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who means to pass down lasting good must take counsel with the realm itself.”

sentences.zh: 故天之聰明，自我人之聰明。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven’s keen hearing and clear sight come from our people’s keen hearing and clear sight.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hears and sees through the ears and eyes of the people.”

sentences.zh: 秦、魏欲獨擅其威，而財得沒其身；

translations.literal: Qin and Wei wished alone to monopolize their awesomeness, and in the end got only the drowning of their persons;
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Cao Wei tried to hoard all authority and perished with it.”

sentences.zh: 周、漢能分其利，而親疏為之用。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han were able to divide its benefit, and close and distant were employed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han prospered by sharing power so that both kin and ministers could serve the throne.”

sentences.zh: 此自聖主之深慮，日月之所照。

translations.literal: This is from the sage ruler’s deep planning, what sun and moon shine upon.
translations.idiomatic: That is the far-sighted policy of a true king, plain as sunlight.”

sentences.zh: 事雖淺，當深謀之；

translations.literal: Although the affair is shallow, one ought to plan it deeply;
translations.idiomatic: Even a small matter deserves deep thought.”

sentences.zh: 言雖輕，當重思之。

translations.literal: although the words are light, one ought to ponder them heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Even casual words should be weighed with care.”

sentences.zh: 志備位儒官，若言不及禮，是志寇竊。

translations.literal: Zhi occupies a place among Confucian officials; if his words do not reach to ritual, then Zhi is a bandit-thief.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a scholar’s title: if I stay silent on a question of ritual, I am nothing but a thief of office.”

sentences.zh: 知忠不言，議所不敢。

translations.literal: To know loyalty and not speak—this is what, in deliberation, I dare not.
translations.idiomatic: To see what is right and hold my tongue is what I dare not do.”

sentences.zh: 志以為當如博士等議。

translations.literal: Zhi holds that it ought to be as the erudits and others deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty should accept the erudits’ opinion.”

sentences.zh: 」議成當上，見其從弟高邑公嘉。

translations.literal: ” When the deliberation was completed and was about to be submitted, he saw his younger male cousin, Duke of Gaoyi, Jia.
translations.idiomatic: When the draft was finished and ready for the throne, he met his cousin Cao Jia, Duke of Gaoyi.”

sentences.zh: 嘉曰：「兄議甚切，百年之後必書晉史，目下將見責邪。

translations.literal: Jia said, “Elder brother’s deliberation is very cutting; after a hundred years it will certainly be written in the Jin history; presently will you be blamed?”
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jia warned him, “Brother, this memorial cuts deep. Future historians will praise you, but what about the emperor’s anger today?”

sentences.zh: 」帝覽議，大怒曰：「曹志尚不明吾心，況四海乎！

translations.literal: ” When the emperor perused the deliberation, he was greatly angry and said, “If Cao Zhi still does not clarify Our heart, how much less all within the four seas!”
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read it, he flew into a rage. “If Cao Zhi cannot read my mind,” he cried, “what can I expect of the rest of the realm?”

sentences.zh: 」以議者不指答所問，橫造異論，策免太常鄭默。

translations.literal: ” Because the deliberators did not pointedly answer what was asked, but recklessly produced contrary discussions, by edict he dismissed Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Because the memorialists had ignored the question put to them and veered into dissent, he removed Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo by edict.”

sentences.zh: 於是有司奏收志等結罪，詔惟免志官，以公還第，其餘皆付廷尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the relevant officials memorialized to seize Zhi and others and bind their crimes; an edict only removed Zhi from office, returning him as duke to his residence; the rest were all handed over to the commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials asked to arrest Cao Zhi and his allies on conspiracy charges. The emperor stripped only Cao Zhi of office and sent him home as a duke, while the others were remanded to the commandant of justice.”

sentences.zh: 頃之，志復為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long, Zhi again became Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Cao Zhi was reappointed Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪過禮，因此篤病，喜怒失常。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother; in observing mourning he exceeded the rites, and because of this fell seriously ill, joy and anger were not normal.
translations.idiomatic: His mother’s death left him mourning beyond the prescribed rites; he fell gravely ill and lost control of his moods.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，太常奏以惡諡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; the Minister of Ceremonies submitted that he be given a bad posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the era (probably 288). The Ministry of Ceremonies proposed a harsh posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 崔褒歎曰：「魏顆不從亂，以病為亂故也。

translations.literal: Cui Bao sighed and said, “Wei Ke did not follow disorder; because of illness it was taken as disorder.”
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bao objected: “Wei Ke earned a fair posthumous title because his disobedience had not been mutiny but illness mistaken for mutiny.”

sentences.zh: 今諡曹志而諡其病，豈謂其病不為亂乎！

translations.literal: Now in giving a posthumous title to Cao Zhi and posthumously titling his illness, does it mean that his illness was not disorder!”
translations.idiomatic: If you name Cao Zhi’s sickness ‘rebellion,’ are you saying his sickness was not a kind of rebellion against good order?”

sentences.zh: 」於是諡為定。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the posthumous title was fixed as Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore settled on the posthumous name “Ding” (“the Determined”).”

sentences.zh: 庾峻

translations.literal: Yu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun

sentences.zh: 庾峻，字山甫，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jun, courtesy name Shanfu, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun, style Shanfu, was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖乘，才學洽聞，漢司徒辟，有道征，皆不就。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng, talent and learning broad in hearing, was summoned by the Han Minister of Education, was summoned on account of moral conduct, and in all cases did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Cheng was learned and widely read. The Han court summoned him as Minister of Education and again as a man of recognized virtue; he declined both calls.

sentences.zh: 伯父嶷，中正簡素，仕魏為太僕。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Yi, impartial and upright, simple and plain, served Wei as Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yu Yi, a plain and upright local evaluator, served Wei as Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 父道，廉退貞固，養志不仕。

translations.literal: His father Dao, incorrupt and retiring, chaste and firm, nurtured his aims and did not serve in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Dao lived modestly and refused every office, intent on cultivating his own integrity.

sentences.zh: 牛馬有踶齧者，恐傷人，不貨於市。

translations.literal: If oxen or horses kicked or bit, fearing they would injure people, he did not sell them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He would not sell at market any ox or horse known to kick or bite, lest it harm someone.

sentences.zh: 及諸子貴，賜拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When his various sons became noble, he was granted appointment as Grand Palace Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: When his sons rose to high rank, the court honored him with the title of Grand Palace Grandee.

sentences.zh: 峻少好學，有才思。

translations.literal: Jun in youth loved learning and had talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun loved learning from youth and showed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 嘗游京師，聞魏散騎常侍蘇林老疾在家，往候之。

translations.literal: He once traveled to the capital; hearing that Wei Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Su Lin was old and ill at home, he went to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Luoyang he heard that the Wei scholar Su Lin lay old and sick at home, and called on him.

sentences.zh: 林嘗就乘學，見峻流涕，良久曰：「尊祖高才而性退讓，慈和泛愛，清靜寡欲，不營當世，惟修德行而已。

translations.literal: Lin had once gone to Cheng to study; seeing Jun he wept, and after a long while said, “Your honored grandfather had high talent but a nature of yielding and modesty, kind harmony and universal love, pure quiet and few desires, did not scheme for the present age, only cultivated virtue and conduct, that is all.”
translations.idiomatic: Su Lin had once studied under Yu Cheng. Seeing Yu Jun, he wept and said at length, “Your grandfather was a man of towering gifts yet humble temper—kind, generous, quiet, and free of ambition. He never angled for place; he only perfected his character.”

sentences.zh: 鄢陵舊五六萬戶，聞今裁有數百。

translations.literal: Yanling formerly had fifty or sixty thousand households; I hear that now it is cut down to only several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling once counted fifty or sixty thousand households; today barely a few hundred remain.”

sentences.zh: 君二父孩抱經亂，獨至今日，尊伯為當世令器，君兄弟復俊茂，此尊祖積德之所由也。」

translations.literal: Your two fathers, in infancy embraced, passed through chaos, alone reaching this day; your honored uncle is a fine vessel of the present age; you, elder and younger brothers, again are outstanding and luxuriant—this is what comes from your honored grandfather’s accumulated virtue.”
translations.idiomatic: Your two fathers were carried as infants through the wars yet lived to see this day; your uncle is one of the age’s finest men; you and your brothers shine with promise—this is the harvest of your grandfather’s hidden virtue.”

sentences.zh: 曆郡功曹，舉計掾，州辟從事。

translations.literal: He passed through commandery merit assessor, was recommended as accounting clerk, was summoned by the province as retainer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commandery merit assessor, was recommended as accounting clerk for the capital report, and was hired as a provincial retainer.

sentences.zh: 太常鄭袤見峻，大奇之，舉為博士。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mao saw Jun and greatly marveled at him, recommended him as erudit.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mao, Minister of Ceremonies, was so struck by him that he nominated Yu Jun as an erudit.

sentences.zh: 時重《莊》《老》而輕《經》《史》，駿懼雅道陵遲，乃潛心儒典。

translations.literal: At the time Zhuangzi and Laozi were esteemed while the classics and histories were slighted; Yu Jun feared the correct Way would decline, and therefore immersed his mind in Confucian canons.
translations.idiomatic: When fashionable opinion exalted Zhuangzi and Laozi at the expense of the classics and histories, Yu Jun feared the loss of true culture and threw himself into Confucian study.

sentences.zh: 屬高貴鄉公幸太學，問《尚書》義于峻，峻援引師說，發明經旨，申暢疑滯，對答詳悉。

translations.literal: It fell that the Duke of Gaoxiang visited the National University and asked Jun about the meaning of the Documents; Jun cited and drew on masters’ explanations, opened and clarified the classics’ purport, extended and smoothed doubtful blockages, and answered in detail and exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Cao Mao of Gaoxiang visited the National University and questioned him on the *Book of Documents*, Yu Jun drew on his teachers’ glosses, unfolded knotty passages, and answered with meticulous clarity.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 長安有大獄，久不決，拜峻侍御史，往斷之，朝野稱允。

translations.literal: In Chang’an there was a great prison case, long unsettled; Jun was appointed Attendant Censor and sent to decide it; court and countryside praised it as fair.
translations.idiomatic: A major criminal case at Chang’an had dragged on unresolved; Yu Jun was named Attendant Censor and sent to settle it, and both court and commoners approved his judgment.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，賜爵關中侯，遷司空長史，轉秘書監、御史中丞，拜侍中，加諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was granted noble rank as Marquis Within the Passes, was promoted Minister of Works chief clerk, was transferred Palace Library supervisor and palace assistant secretary, was appointed palace attendant, and was added Grandee Remonstrant.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu took the throne Yu Jun received the rank of Marquis Within the Passes, rose to chief clerk to the Minister of Works, then served as director of the Palace Library and as palace assistant secretary, became a palace attendant, and was given the additional title of Grandee Remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 常侍帝講《詩》，中庶子何劭論《風》《雅》正變之義，峻起難往反，四坐莫能屈之。

translations.literal: He constantly attended the emperor’s exposition of the Odes; Palace Attendant He Shao discussed the meaning of orthodox and changed in the Airs and Elegances; Jun rose and challenged back and forth, and those seated on four sides none could bend him.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly joined the emperor’s lectures on the *Classic of Poetry*. When He Shao, the junior mentor to the heir apparent, spoke on “orthodox” and “mutated” poems in the *Airs* and *Elegances*, Yu Jun rose to debate him to and fro, and no one in the hall could get the better of him.

sentences.zh: 是時風俗趣競，禮讓陵遲。

translations.literal: At that time customs tended to competition, ritual yielding was in decline.
translations.idiomatic: The age chased after rivalry and politeness had worn thin.

sentences.zh: 峻上疏曰：

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun therefore presented a long memorial that began:

sentences.zh: 又疾世浮華，不修名實，著論以非之，文繁不載。

translations.literal: Further he hated the age’s flashiness, not cultivating name and substance; he composed a treatise to criticize it; the text was prolix and is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He also despised hollow display and the neglect of genuine reputation, and wrote a lengthy essay against it—the text is omitted here as too long.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，詔賜朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; an edict granted one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, and three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year (293). The court sent a full set of court robes, another suit, and three hundred thousand cash for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 臨終，敕子瑉朝卒夕殯，幅巾布衣，葬勿擇日。

translations.literal: Facing the end, he instructed his son Min: morning die, evening encoffin; headwrap cloth and plain clothes; bury, do not select a day.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his son Yu Min to bury him the same evening he died, in plain cloth and headcloth, without waiting to choose a lucky day.

sentences.zh: 瑉奉遵遺命，斂以時服。

translations.literal: Min received and followed the dying commands; he was shrouded in timely clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min obeyed: the body was dressed only in everyday clothes.

sentences.zh: 二子：瑉、敳。

translations.literal: Two sons: Min and Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yu Min and Yu Ai.

translations.literal: Equals sign (typographical artifact in the received edition).
translations.idiomatic: The edition prints a stray equals sign between subsections.

sentences.zh: 子瑉

translations.literal: Son Min.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yu Min

sentences.zh: =瑉字子琚。

translations.literal: Equals sign: Min, courtesy name Ziju.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min, courtesy name Ziju, was his son.

sentences.zh: 性淳和好學，行己忠恕。

translations.literal: By nature pure and harmonious, loving learning, in conducting himself loyal and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle, studious, and lived by loyalty and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 少曆散騎常侍、本國中正、侍中，封長岑男。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, impartial and upright of his native state, palace attendant, was enfeoffed as Baron of Changcen.
translations.idiomatic: While young he served as Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, local merit evaluator for his commandery, and palace attendant, and was ennobled as Baron of Changcen.

sentences.zh: 懷帝之沒劉元海也，瑉從在平陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai was lost to Liu Yuanhai, Min followed and was at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai fell into the hands of Liu Yuan (Liu Yuanhai), Yu Min followed him to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 元海大會，因使帝行酒，瑉不勝悲憤，再拜上酒，因大號哭，賊惡之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai held a great gathering; thereupon he made the emperor pour wine; Min could not bear grief and anger, twice bowed and presented wine, thereupon loudly wailed and wept; the bandits hated him.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Liu Yuan ordered the captive emperor to pour wine for the guests. Yu Min, unable to contain his grief, presented the cup with a formal bow and broke into loud weeping; the conquerors detested him for it.

sentences.zh: 會有告瑉及王儁等謀應劉琨者，元海因圖弑逆，瑉等並遇害。

translations.literal: It happened that there was one who reported Min and Wang Jun and others plotting to respond to Liu Kun; Yuanhai therefore plotted regicide and rebellion; Min and others together met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Yu Min, Wang Jun, and others of plotting to aid Liu Kun. Liu Yuan seized on the charge to frame them for regicide, and Yu Min was executed with the rest.

sentences.zh: 初，洛陽之未陷也，瑉為侍中，直於省內，謂同僚許遐曰：「世路如此，禍難將及，吾當死乎此屋耳！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Luoyang had not yet fallen, Min was palace attendant, on duty inside the department; he said to colleague Xu Xia, “The age’s road is thus; disaster is about to arrive; I ought to die in this house!”
translations.idiomatic: Before Luoyang fell, Yu Min was on duty in the palace as palace attendant. He told his colleague Xu Xia, “The times are turning this dark—trouble is coming. I expect to die in this very hall!”

sentences.zh: 」及是，竟不免焉。

translations.literal: ” When it came to this, in the end he did not escape.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he could not escape that fate.”

sentences.zh: 太元末，追諡曰貞。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taiyuan era, posthumously he was titled Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taiyuan era (376–396) the court posthumously titled him “Zhen” (“the Upright”).

translations.literal: Equals sign printed in the edition.
translations.idiomatic: The edition inserts a stray equals sign between subsections.

sentences.zh: 瑉弟敳

translations.literal: Min’s younger brother Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min’s brother, Yu Kai

sentences.zh: =敳字子嵩。

translations.literal: Equals sign: Kai, courtesy name Zisong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai, courtesy name Zisong, was his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 長不滿七尺，而腰帶十圍，雅有遠韻。

translations.literal: In height he did not fill seven chi, yet his waist belt was ten spans around; elegantly he had a distant tone.
translations.idiomatic: He stood under seven feet tall yet girt his waist with ten hand-spans of belt, carrying an air of lofty detachment.

sentences.zh: 為陳留相，未嘗以事嬰心，從容酣暢，寄通而已。

translations.literal: As chancellor of Chenliu, he never let affairs cling to his mind; at ease he was merry and free, entrusting penetration and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor of Chenliu he never let paperwork fret him; he moved through office in relaxed ease, letting things take their own course.

sentences.zh: 處眾人中，居然獨立。

translations.literal: Placed among a multitude of people, he stood alone as if apart.
translations.idiomatic: In any crowd he seemed to stand apart, self-contained.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀《老》《莊》，曰：「正與人意暗同。

translations.literal: He once read the Laozi and Zhuangzi and said, “They exactly match people’s thoughts in hidden sameness.”
translations.idiomatic: Reading the *Laozi* and *Zhuangzi*, he remarked, “These texts voice what we already feel without knowing it.”

sentences.zh: 」太尉王衍雅重之。

translations.literal: ” Grand Commandant Wang Yan greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 敳見王室多難，終知嬰禍，乃著《意賦》以豁情，猶賈誼之《服鳥》也。

translations.literal: Kai saw the royal house had many difficulties, and in the end knew he would encounter disaster; thereupon he composed the “Rhapsody on Intent” to open his feelings, like Jia Yi’s “The Owl.”
translations.idiomatic: Seeing endless trouble for the throne, Yu Kai knew he would be swept up in it, so he wrote the *Rhapsody on Intent* to clear his heart, much as Jia Yi once wrote *The Owl*.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「至理歸於渾一兮，榮辱固亦同貫。

translations.literal: Its words said, “The utmost pattern returns to undivided oneness; glory and shame are of one thread.”
translations.idiomatic: It begins: “The highest truth folds back into the undivided whole; honor and disgrace run on the same string.”

sentences.zh: 存亡既已均齊兮，正盡死復何歎。

translations.literal: Survival and loss already being equalized, when uprightness is exhausted at death, what again is there to sigh for.
translations.idiomatic: Life and death already balance one another; when integrity is spent in dying, what is left to lament?”

sentences.zh: 物咸定于無初兮，俟時至而後驗。

translations.literal: Things all are fixed in having no beginning; await the time’s arrival and afterward verify.
translations.idiomatic: All things rest in a beginningless fixity; only when the moment comes is the pattern proved.”

sentences.zh: 若四節之素代兮，豈當今之得遠？

translations.literal: Like the four seasons’ plain alternation—how could the present attain distance from it?
translations.idiomatic: They turn like the four seasons in their steady round—how could the present hour escape that wheel?”

sentences.zh: 且安有壽之與夭兮，或者情橫多戀。

translations.literal: Moreover how can there be long life versus early death? Perhaps feeling runs wild with much attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Where is the line between a full span and an early end? Passion clings where reason should let go.”

sentences.zh: 宗統竟初不別兮，大德亡其情願。

translations.literal: Ancestral continuity in the end is not distinct from the start; great virtue loses its emotional wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Lineage and extinction are one at root; the greatest power forgets what the heart prefers.”

sentences.zh: 蠢動皆神之為兮，癡聖惟質所建。

translations.literal: Wriggling movement is all the work of spirit; foolishness and sageliness are what substance establishes.
translations.idiomatic: Every twitch of life is spirit’s play; fool and sage alike are shaped by the same stuff.”

sentences.zh: 真人都遣穢累兮，性茫蕩而無岸。

translations.literal: The perfected person all casts off foul accumulations; nature is vast and boundless without shore.
translations.idiomatic: The realized man sheds every stain; his nature is shoreless, open sky.”

sentences.zh: 縱驅於遼廓之庭兮，委體乎寂寥之館。

translations.literal: Let loose and driven in the courtyard of vast distance; entrust the body to the lodge of silence and emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: He ranges the court of boundless space and lodges his body in utter stillness.”

sentences.zh: 天地短於朝生兮，億代促於始旦。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are shorter than a morning’s birth; a hundred million ages are hurried compared to the first dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are briefer than the mayfly’s dawn; eons shrink beside the first light.”

sentences.zh: 顧瞻宇宙微細兮，眇若豪鋒之半。

translations.literal: Looking back at the universe’s minuteness, it is tiny like half a hair tip’s point.
translations.idiomatic: Look back on the cosmos and it is smaller than half a spearpoint’s gleam.”

sentences.zh: 飄搖玄曠之域兮，深漠暢而靡玩。

translations.literal: Drifting in the dark vastness’s region; deep and silent, free-flowing and without plaything.
translations.idiomatic: He drifts the dark expanse, depth without bottom, freedom without a toy to grasp.”

sentences.zh: 兀與自然並體兮，融液忽而四散。

translations.literal: Towering, with spontaneity sharing one body; melting and flowing, suddenly scattering in four directions.
translations.idiomatic: He stands with Nature as one body, then melts and scatters like dew on the wind.”

sentences.zh: 」從子亮見賦，問曰：「若有意也，非賦所盡；

translations.literal: ” His nephew Liang saw the rhapsody and asked, “If there is intent, it is not what a rhapsody can exhaust;
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yu Liang read the piece and asked, “If you really mean this, no poem can say it all;

sentences.zh: 若無意也，復何所賦？

translations.literal: If there is no intent, what again is there to rhapsodize?”
translations.idiomatic: if you do not, why bother writing a rhapsody at all?”

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「在有無之間耳！」

translations.literal: ” He answered, “It is between having and not having, that is all!”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai answered, “Somewhere between caring and not caring—that is all.”

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 是時天下多故，機變屢起，敳常靜默無為。

translations.literal: At that time all under Heaven had many troubles; stratagems and shifts arose repeatedly; Kai constantly was still and silent and non-active.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in constant upheaval and intrigue, yet Yu Kai stayed quiet and let events run their course.

sentences.zh: 參東海王越太傅軍事，轉軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: He joined Prince of the Eastern Seas Yue’s Grand Mentor military affairs, was transferred army consultation libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff of Sima Yue, Prince of the Eastern Seas, as Grand Mentor, then became army advisory libationer.

sentences.zh: 時越府多雋異，敳在其中，常自袖手。

translations.literal: At that time Yue’s bureau had many outstanding and unusual men; Kai was among them, and constantly kept his own hands in his sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue’s headquarters teemed with brilliant men, but Yu Kai usually stood by with his hands tucked in his sleeves.

sentences.zh: 豫州牧長史河南郭象善《老》《莊》，時人以為王弼之亞。

translations.literal: Chief clerk to the governor of Yuzhou, Guo Xiang of Henan, was good at the Laozi and Zhuangzi; people of the time considered him second only to Wang Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang of Henan, chief clerk on the staff of the governor of Yuzhou, was a master of the *Laozi* and *Zhuangzi* whom contemporaries ranked just below Wang Bi.

sentences.zh: 敳甚知之，每曰：「郭子玄何必減瘐子嵩」。

translations.literal: Kai understood him very much, and each time said, “Guo Zixuan need not be less than Yu Zisong.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai understood him well and used to say, “Guo Zixuan is nobody’s inferior to Yu Zisong.”

sentences.zh: 象後為太傅主簿，任事專勢。

translations.literal: Xiang later became Grand Mentor chief clerk, handling affairs with sole power.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as chief clerk to the Grand Mentor, Guo Xiang monopolized influence over every decision.

sentences.zh: 敳謂象曰：「卿自是當世大才，我疇昔之意都已盡矣。」

translations.literal: Kai said to Xiang, “You yourself are a great talent of the present age; my former intent toward you is all exhausted.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai told him, “You are a leading talent of our day; whatever regard I once had for you is spent.”

sentences.zh: 敳有重名，為搢紳所推，而聚斂積實，談者譏之。

translations.literal: Kai had a weighty name, was pushed forward by the gentry-belted, yet amassed and gathered solid wealth; those who talked ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai enjoyed great reputation among the official class, yet he hoarded wealth, and gossips mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 都官從事溫嶠奏之，敳更器嶠，目嶠森森如千丈松，雖礧砢多節，施之大廈，有棟樑之用。

translations.literal: Capital official retainer Wen Qiao memorialized against him; Kai all the more esteemed Qiao, eyed Qiao as forest-tall like a thousand-foot pine, although gnarled with many knots, applied to a great hall, having the use of a ridgepole beam.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Qiao, a capital investigator, impeached him, Yu Kai only respected Wen the more, likening him to a towering pine—gnarled and knotty, yet timber fit to roof a palace.

sentences.zh: 時劉輿見任于越，人士多為所構，惟敳縱心事外，無跡可間。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu was employed by Yue; gentlemen mostly were framed by him; only Kai let his mind roam outside matters, without traces by which to be separated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu then held Sima Yue’s confidence and ruined many colleagues, but Yu Kai kept his heart beyond reach and left no handle for intrigue.

sentences.zh: 後以其性儉家富，說越令就換錢千萬，冀其有吝，因此可乘。

translations.literal: Later because his nature was frugal and his family rich, they persuaded Yue to order him to exchange cash to the amount of ten million, hoping he would be stingy, and by this could be taken advantage of.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his miserly habits and great wealth, someone urged Sima Yue to demand ten million cash from him in exchange, hoping stinginess would give them a pretext to strike.

sentences.zh: 越于眾坐中問於敳，而敳乃穨然已醉，幘墮機上，以頭就穿取，徐答-{云}-：「下官家有二千萬，隨公所取矣。

translations.literal: Yue in the midst of a public seating asked Kai, but Kai was already collapsed drunk; his headcloth fell on the desk; using his head he went to the hole to take it; slowly answered saying, “This inferior’s household has twenty million; follow the duke’s taking.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue put the demand to him in open court. Yu Kai was already slumped in drink; his cap slipped onto the table and he fished it back with his forehead before drawling, “I keep twenty million at home—take what you will.”

sentences.zh: 」輿於是乃服。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Yu was convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu conceded defeat.

sentences.zh: 越甚悅，因曰：「不可以小人之慮度君子之心。

translations.literal: Yue was greatly pleased, and thereupon said, “One must not measure a gentleman’s heart with a petty man’s thoughts.”
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue was delighted and said, “Never measure a gentleman’s mind with a petty man’s suspicions.”

sentences.zh: 」王衍不與敳交，敳卿之不置。

translations.literal: ” Wang Yan did not associate with Kai; Kai kept calling him qing without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan refused his friendship, yet Yu Kai showered him with the intimate pronoun *qing* at every turn.”

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「君不得為耳。

translations.literal: Yan said, “You cannot do it, that is all.”
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan said, “You simply will not drop it.”

sentences.zh: 」敳曰：「卿自君我，我自卿卿。

translations.literal: ” Kai said, “You yourself lord me; I myself qing-qing you.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai retorted, “You may address me as ‘lord’ if you wish; I shall keep calling you *qing*.”

sentences.zh: 我自用我家法，卿自用卿家法。

translations.literal: I myself use my family’s rules; you yourself use your family’s rules.”
translations.idiomatic: I follow my house’s etiquette; you follow yours.”

sentences.zh: 」衍甚奇之。

translations.literal: ” Yan greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was struck with admiration.

sentences.zh: 石勒之亂，與衍俱被害，時年五十。

translations.literal: In Shi Le’s rebellion, together with Yan he met harm; at the time his age was fifty.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le rose, Yu Kai died alongside Wang Yan at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 郭象

translations.literal: Guo Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang

sentences.zh: 郭象，字子玄，少有才理，好《老》《莊》，能清言。

translations.literal: Guo Xiang, courtesy name Zixuan, in youth had talent in pattern-principle, loved the Laozi and Zhuangzi, was able in pure talk.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang, style Zixuan, showed early brilliance in speculative thought, loved the *Laozi* and *Zhuangzi*, and excelled at *qingtan* discourse.

sentences.zh: 太尉王衍每云：「聽象語，如懸河瀉水，注而不竭。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Yan always said, “Listening to Xiang’s words is like a suspended river pouring water, pouring in without exhaustion.”
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan used to say, “Hearing Guo Xiang speak is like watching a cataract pour—never running dry.”

sentences.zh: 」州郡辟召，不就。

translations.literal: ” Provinces and commanderies summoned him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery posts were offered; he declined them all.

sentences.zh: 常閒居，以文論自娛。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt in leisure, using literary essays to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly at home, amusing himself with essays.

sentences.zh: 後辟司徒掾，稍至黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as retainer to the Minister of Education, gradually reaching Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accepted appointment as a retainer to the Minister of Education and rose step by step to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 東海王越引為太傅主簿，甚見親委，遂任職當權，熏灼內外，由是素論去之。

translations.literal: Prince of the Eastern Seas Yue drew him in as Grand Mentor chief clerk; he was greatly seen as intimate and entrusted; thereupon holding office he grasped power, fuming and scorching within and without; because of this plain opinion departed from him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, Prince of the Eastern Seas, made him chief clerk to the Grand Mentor and leaned on him so heavily that he dominated court and camp alike, until men of principle turned away.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末病卒，著碑論十二篇。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongjia era he died of illness; he composed twelve pieces of stele treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness near the end of the Yongjia era (307–313), leaving twelve commemorative essays.

sentences.zh: 先是，注《莊子》者數十家，莫能究其旨統。

translations.literal: Earlier, those who annotated the Zhuangzi were several tens of houses; none could exhaust its purport’s continuity.
translations.idiomatic: Before his time dozens of scholars had glossed the *Zhuangzi*, yet none had mastered its overarching design.

sentences.zh: 向秀於舊注外而為解義，妙演奇致，大暢玄風，惟《秋水》、《至樂》二篇未竟而秀卒。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiu outside old annotations made explanatory meanings, wondrously unfolding strange reaches, greatly opening the dark wind; only the two chapters “Autumn Floods” and “Perfect Enjoyment” were not completed and Xiu died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiu went beyond older commentaries with interpretations of rare subtlety that gave Dark Learning its fullest voice, but he died before finishing *Autumn Floods* and *Perfect Enjoyment*.

sentences.zh: 秀子幼，其義零落，然頗有別本遷流。

translations.literal: Xiu’s son was young; its meanings were scattered and fallen, yet there were rather alternate copies that drifted about.
translations.idiomatic: His son was too young to preserve the work, and the text survived only in scattered copies.

sentences.zh: 象為人行薄，以秀義不傳於世，遂竊以為己注，乃自注《秋水》、《至樂》二篇，又易《馬蹄》一篇，其餘眾篇或點定文句而巳。

translations.literal: Xiang’s conduct was mean; because Xiu’s meanings were not transmitted in the generation, he thereupon stole them to make his own annotations; then he himself annotated the two chapters “Autumn Floods” and “Perfect Enjoyment,” again altered the one chapter “Horse’s Hoofs”; as for the rest of the many chapters, he merely dotted and settled phrases and sentences, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang was a man of shallow character. Seeing that Xiang Xiu’s gloss had not reached print, he appropriated it as his own, supplied the missing chapters *Autumn Floods* and *Perfect Enjoyment*, rewrote *Horse’s Hoofs*, and merely touched up the rest.

sentences.zh: 其後秀義別本出，故今有向、郭二《莊》，其義一也。

translations.literal: Afterward Xiu’s meaning’s alternate copy appeared; therefore today there are two Zhuangzis, Xiang’s and Guo’s; their meaning is one.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Xiu’s original eventually surfaced, the world found two *Zhuangzi* commentaries, Xiang’s and Guo’s, teaching the same doctrine.

sentences.zh: 庾純

translations.literal: Yu Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun

sentences.zh: 庾純，字謀甫，博學有才義，為世儒宗。

translations.literal: Yu Chun, courtesy name Moufu, broadly learned and with talent in moral principle, was for the generation the Confucians’ ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun, style Moufu, was widely read, gifted in argument, and honored as a dean among Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 郡補主簿，仍參征南府，累遷黃門侍郎，封關內侯，曆中書令、河南尹。

translations.literal: The commandery supplemented him as chief clerk, still joined the south-conquering headquarters, was repeatedly promoted Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, was enfeoffed Marquis Within the Passes, passed through Palace Secretary and Henan intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as commandery chief clerk, joined the staff of the south-campaign command, rose to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, was ennobled Marquis Within the Passes, and served as palace secretary and intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，純以賈充奸佞，與任愷共舉充西鎮關中，充由是不平。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chun because Jia Chong was treacherous and flattering, together with Ren Kai jointly recommended Chong to go west and garrison Guanzhong; Chong from this was not level.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, deeming Jia Chong a sycophant, Yu Chun joined Ren Kai in urging that Jia be posted west to guard Guanzhong—an advice that earned Jia’s lasting resentment.

sentences.zh: 充嘗宴朝士，而純後至，充謂曰：「君行常居人前，今何以在後？

translations.literal: Chong once feasted court gentlemen, but Chun arrived late; Chong said to him, “Your conduct always places you before people; now why are you behind?”
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet for courtiers Jia Chong noticed Yu Chun arrive last and jibed, “You usually push to the front—what keeps you at the rear today?”

sentences.zh: 」純曰：「旦有小市井事不了，是以來後。

translations.literal: ” Chun said, “This morning there were small market-ward matters not finished; therefore I came late.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun answered, “A trifling market errand detained me this morning.”

sentences.zh: 」世言純之先嘗有伍伯者，充之先有市魁者，充、純以此相譏焉。

translations.literal: ” World talk said Chun’s ancestor once had a ward-chief; Chong’s ancestor had a market chief; Chong and Chun by this mocked each other.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip said Yu Chun’s forebears had been market bailiffs and Jia Chong’s had been ward bosses—each man used the taunt against the other.”

sentences.zh: 充自以位隆望重，意殊不平。

translations.literal: Chong himself because his position was lofty and his repute weighty, his intent was especially not level.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong, confident in his rank and prestige, nursed a deeper grudge.

sentences.zh: 及純行酒，充不時飲。

translations.literal: When Chun poured wine, Chong did not drink in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chun circulated the cup, Jia Chong refused to drink at once.

sentences.zh: 純曰：「長者為壽，何敢爾乎！

translations.literal: Chun said, “The elder raises a toast—how dare it be thus!”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun said, “An elder offers you a toast—how dare you slight it?”

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「父老不歸供養，將何言也！

translations.literal: ” Chong said, “The father is old and you do not return to support and nurture—what words are there to say!”
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong shot back, “Your father is aged and you will not go home to care for him—what right have you to lecture me?”

sentences.zh: 」純因發怒曰：「賈充！

translations.literal: ” Chun thereupon grew angry and said, “Jia Chong!”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun burst out, “Jia Chong!”

sentences.zh: 天下凶凶，由爾一人。

translations.literal: All under Heaven is in turmoil; it is because of you alone.”
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in chaos, and you alone are to blame.”

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「充輔佐二世，蕩平巴、蜀，有何罪而天下為之凶凶？

translations.literal: ” Chong said, “Chong has assisted two generations, swept and pacified Ba and Shu—what crime is there that all under Heaven for it is in turmoil?”
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong retorted, “I have served two reigns and helped pacify Ba and Shu—what crime makes me responsible for the world’s turmoil?”

sentences.zh: 」純曰：「高貴鄉公何在？

translations.literal: ” Chun said, “Where is the Duke of Gaoxiang?”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun answered, “Where is the Duke of Gaoxiang?”

sentences.zh: 」眾坐因罷。

translations.literal: ” The seated assembly thereupon broke up.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet broke up in disorder.

sentences.zh: 充左右欲執純，中護軍羊琇、侍中王濟佑之，因得出。

translations.literal: Chong’s attendants wished to seize Chun; Central Army Guard Yang Xiu and Palace Attendant Wang Ji protected him; thereby he was able to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong’s guards moved to arrest Yu Chun, but Yang Xiu and Wang Ji shielded him until he escaped the hall.

sentences.zh: 充慚怒，上表解職。

translations.literal: Chong was ashamed and angry, submitted a memorial requesting to resign office.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and furious, Jia Chong memorialized to resign his posts.

sentences.zh: 純懼，上河南尹、關內侯印綬，上表自劾曰：

translations.literal: Chun was afraid, submitted the Henan intendant and Marquis Within the Passes seals and ribbons, submitted a memorial impeaching himself, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisal, Yu Chun returned the seals of Henan intendant and Marquis Within the Passes and filed a self-accusation that read:

sentences.zh: 御史中丞孔恂劾純，請免官。

translations.literal: Palace assistant secretary Kong Xun impeached Chun, requesting removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace assistant secretary Kong Xun impeached him and asked that he be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先王崇尊卑之禮，明貴賤之序，著溫克之德，記沈酗之禍，所以光宣道化，示人軌儀也。

translations.literal: An edict said, “The former kings honored high-and-low ritual, clarified noble-and-base order, wrote the virtue of gentle restraint, recorded the disaster of sinking in drunkenness—by this they were to brighten and spread the Way’s transformation, to show people tracks and models.”
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: “The ancient kings exalted hierarchy, fixed rank, praised gentle self-command, and warned against drunken excess—all to spread moral teaching and set a pattern for the people.”

sentences.zh: 昔廣漢陵慢宰相，獲犯上之刑；

translations.literal: Formerly Guanghan treated the chancellor with contempt and received the punishment of offending superiors;
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan once insulted a chancellor and paid with his life for lèse-majesté;

sentences.zh: 灌夫托醉肆忿，致誅斃之罪。

translations.literal: Guan Fu relied on drunkenness to unleash resentment, brought about the crime of execution and killing.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu feigned drunken rage and earned execution.

sentences.zh: 純以凡才，備位卿尹，不惟謙敬之節，不忌覆車之戒，陵上無禮，悖言自口，宜加顯黜，以肅朝倫。

translations.literal: Chun with ordinary talent occupies a place among ministers and intendants; he does not think on the demeanor of modest respect, does not fear the warning of the overturned cart; he treats superiors without ritual; perverse words come from his mouth; he should receive clear demotion, in order to rectify court relations.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun, a man of middling ability, holds high office yet shows neither humility nor fear of past warnings; he insulted his superiors and spoke treason from his cup. He should be disgraced and dismissed to restore discipline at court.”

sentences.zh: 」遂免純官。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Chun’s office was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun was therefore stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 又以純父老不求供養，使據禮典正其臧否。

translations.literal: Further because Chun’s father was old and he did not seek to support and nurture, they ordered according to ritual canons to rectify his good or bad.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered a review, under the ritual code, of whether he had failed in caring for his aged father.

sentences.zh: 太傅何曾、太尉荀顗、驃騎將軍齊王攸議曰：「凡斷正臧否，宜先稽之禮、律。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor He Ceng, Grand Commandant Xun Yi, General of Agile Cavalry Prince of Qi You deliberated, saying, “Whenever judging and rectifying good or bad, one ought first to examine ritual and statute.”
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor He Ceng, Grand Commandant Xun Yi, and Sima You, Prince of Qi, jointly ruled: “Questions of right and wrong must be settled against ritual and law.”

sentences.zh: 八十者，一子不從政；

translations.literal: For those eighty, one son does not follow government service;
translations.idiomatic: The code exempts one son from office when a parent reaches eighty;

sentences.zh: 九十者，其家不從政。

translations.literal: for those ninety, his household does not follow government service.
translations.idiomatic: at ninety the whole household may stand aside.”

sentences.zh: 新令亦如之。

translations.literal: The new ordinance is also like this.
translations.idiomatic: The new statutes say the same.

sentences.zh: 按純父年八十一，兄弟六人，三人在家，不廢侍養。

translations.literal: Examining: Chun’s father’s age is eighty-one; brothers are six; three are at home; serving nurture is not neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun’s father is eighty-one; of six brothers, three remain at home, so the father is not left uncared for.

sentences.zh: 純不求供養，其於禮、律未有違也。

translations.literal: That Chun does not seek to support and nurture, as for this in ritual and statute there is not yet violation.
translations.idiomatic: His staying in office therefore breaks neither ritual nor statute.

sentences.zh: 司空公以純備位卿尹，望其有加於人。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works duke because Chun occupies a place among ministers and intendants, hoped that he would have increase toward others.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of works I expected a man of his rank to set a higher example.

sentences.zh: 而純荒醉，肆其忿怒。

translations.literal: Yet Chun was wild drunk, unleashed his angry fury.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he drank himself witless and vented rage in public.

sentences.zh: 臣以為純不遠布孝至之行，而近習常人之失，應在譏貶。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that Chun does not broadly spread utmost filial conduct, yet is near to practicing ordinary people’s faults; he should receive ridicule and demotion.”
translations.idiomatic: I hold that he failed the highest standard of filial example while guilty only of common misconduct; he deserves censure, not the gravest penalties.”

sentences.zh: 」司徒石苞議：「純榮官忘親，惡聞格言，不忠不孝，宜除名削爵土。

translations.literal: ” Minister of Education Shi Bao deliberated: “Chun with glorious office forgot kin, hated hearing model words; not loyal, not filial; should remove name and strip noble territory.”
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Shi Bao argued: “Yu Chun chose office over family and spurned good counsel—disloyal and unfilial. Strip his titles and lands.”

sentences.zh: 」司徒西曹掾劉斌議以為：

translations.literal: ” Minister of Education west bureau retainer Liu Bin deliberated, holding:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin, a western bureau clerk of the Minister of Education, offered another opinion:

sentences.zh: 河南功曹史龐劄等表曰：

translations.literal: Henan merit assessor clerk Pang Zha and others submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Pang Zha and other merit clerks from Henan petitioned:

sentences.zh: 帝復下詔曰：「自中世以來，多為貴重順意，賤者生情，故令釋之、定國得揚名於前世。

translations.literal: The emperor again issued an edict saying, “Since middle ages, mostly for the noble and weighty smooth intention, the base give rise to feeling; therefore it made Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo able to raise their names in former generations.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a further edict: “In recent generations judges have flattered the powerful while venting spite on the humble—yet it was fairness to the lowly that made names like Zhang Shizhi and Yu Dingguo shine in the past.”

sentences.zh: 今議責庾純，不惟溫克，醉酒沈湎，此責人以齊聖也。

translations.literal: Now in deliberation blaming Yu Chun, not only gentle restraint, drunk wine sinking deep—this is blaming people with equalizing sagehood.”
translations.idiomatic: To punish Yu Chun for drunkenness alone, without acknowledging his usual restraint, is to demand common men meet a sage’s standard.”

sentences.zh: 疑賈公亦醉，若其不醉，終不於百客之中責以不去官供養也。

translations.literal: I suspect Duke Jia was also drunk; if he was not drunk, in the end he would not among a hundred guests blame him with not leaving office to support and nurture.”
translations.idiomatic: I suspect Duke Jia was drunk himself; had he been sober he would never have raised the charge of neglecting a parent before a hall full of guests.”

sentences.zh: 大晉依聖人典禮，制臣子出處之宜，若有八十，皆當歸養，亦不獨純也。

translations.literal: Great Jin according to the sages’ ritual canons regulated the propriety of ministers’ and sons’ going out and staying; if there is someone eighty, all ought to return to nurture; nor is it only Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin follows the sages’ ritual code on when a son may serve or stay home: once a parent reaches eighty, any official should retire to care for them—not Yu Chun alone.

sentences.zh: 古人云：'由醉之言，俾出童羖。

translations.literal: The ancients said, ‘From drunk speech, make him produce a hornless ram.’
translations.idiomatic: The classic line runs, ‘Words spoken in drink—take them as the bleating of a black ram.’

sentences.zh: '明不責醉，恐失度也。

translations.literal: ’It clarifies that one does not blame drunkenness, fearing loss of measure.”
translations.idiomatic: That is why wise rulers do not punish drunken slips—they fear to overreach.”

sentences.zh: 所以免純者，當為將來之醉戒耳。

translations.literal: The reason for pardoning Chun ought to be as a warning for future drunkenness, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun is pardoned as a precedent for how the court will treat future brawls over wine.”

sentences.zh: 齊王、劉掾議當矣。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi and Clerk Liu’s deliberation is correct.”
translations.idiomatic: The opinions of Prince Sima You and Clerk Liu Bin should prevail.”

sentences.zh: 」復以純為國子祭酒，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: ”Again they made Chun Libationer of the National University, added Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun was reappointed Libationer of the National University with the added title of Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary.”

sentences.zh: 後將軍荀眅于朝會中奏純以前坐不孝免黜，不宜升進。

translations.literal: General of the Rear Xun Min at a court assembly memorialized that Chun, because he earlier sat for unfilial conduct and was dismissed, was not fit for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: At court General of the Rear Xun Min argued that Yu Chun, once removed for alleged unfilial conduct, should not be promoted again.

sentences.zh: 侍中甄德進曰：「孝以顯親為大，祿養為榮。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhen De advanced and said, “Filial piety takes making parents illustrious as great; salary nurture is glorious.”
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Zhen De replied, “Filial duty means honoring one’s parents; supporting them on an official’s salary is itself a mark of grace.”

sentences.zh: 詔赦純前愆，擢為近侍，兼掌教官，此純召不俟駕之日。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned Chun’s prior fault, raised him to near attendant, concurrently grasping instruction officials; this was Chun’s day of summons without awaiting the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The throne had forgiven his earlier fault, raised him to palace service, and put him over the academicians—the very moment he was summoned without waiting to harness his coach.”

sentences.zh: 而後將軍眅敢以私議貶奪公論，抗言矯情，誣罔朝廷，宜加貶黜。

translations.literal: Yet General of the Rear Min dared with private deliberation to belittle and seize public discussion, to oppose speech and feign feeling, to deceive the court; he should receive demotion and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet General Xun Min used private spite to overturn settled opinion, spoke falsely, and slandered the court—he deserves demotion.”

sentences.zh: 」眅坐免官。

translations.literal: ” Min by sitting was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Min was stripped of his posts.”

sentences.zh: 初，眅與純俱為大將軍所辟，眅整麗車服，純率素而已，眅以為愧恨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Min and Chun together were summoned by the Grand General; Min arranged splendid carriage and dress, Chun was plain and simple only; Min because of this felt ashamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, both had been hired by the Grand General: Xun Min arrived in splendid equipage while Yu Chun came plainly dressed, which left Xun burning with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 至是，毀純。

translations.literal: When it came to this, he slandered Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Now he took revenge by attacking Yu Chun.

sentences.zh: 眅既免黜，純更以此愧之，亟往慰勉之，時人稱純通恕。

translations.literal: When Min was already dismissed, Chun further by this shamed him, repeatedly went to console and encourage him; people of the time praised Chun as comprehensive in forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun Min fell, Yu Chun felt ashamed on his behalf and visited him often to console him—conduct contemporaries praised as generous.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，以父憂去官。

translations.literal: He was promoted palace attendant, because of father mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant but resigned to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 起為御史中丞，轉尚書。

translations.literal: He was raised to be palace assistant secretary, was transferred Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as palace assistant secretary and then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 除魏郡太守，不之官，拜少府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Wei commandery, did not go to the post, was appointed Minister of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Administrator of Wei but never took up the post, and was appointed Minister of the Palace Treasury instead.

sentences.zh: 年六十四卒。

translations.literal: At age sixty-four he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 子旉。

translations.literal: Son Bin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu Bin.

translations.literal: Equals sign in the edition.
translations.idiomatic: The edition prints a stray equals sign.

sentences.zh: 子旉

translations.literal: Son Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yu Bin

sentences.zh: =旉字允臧。

translations.literal: Equals sign: Bin, courtesy name Yuncang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bin, courtesy name Yuncang, was his son.

sentences.zh: 少有清節，歷位博士。

translations.literal: In youth he had pure integrity, passed through posts as erudit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had a reputation for integrity and rose to the post of erudit.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸之就國也，下禮官議崇錫之物。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi You went to his state, he sent down to ritual officials to deliberate the things of honoring and bestowing.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima You of Qi left for his fief, the court ordered ritual officials to decide what honors should attend him.

sentences.zh: 旉與博士太叔廣、劉暾、繆蔚、郭頤、秦秀、傅珍等上表諫曰：

translations.literal: Bin together with erudits Taishu Guang, Liu Tun, Miao Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, Fu Zhen and others submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bin joined Erudits Taishu Guang, Liu Tun, Miao Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, Fu Zhen, and others in a memorial of protest that began:

sentences.zh: 旉草議，先以呈父純，純不禁。

translations.literal: Bin drafted the deliberation, first presented it to his father Chun; Chun did not forbid.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bin drafted the memorial and showed it first to his father, who raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 太常鄭默、博士祭酒曹志並過其事。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo and Libationer Cao Zhi both passed through the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Mo and Libationer Cao Zhi were drawn into the same affair.

sentences.zh: 武帝以博士不答所問，答所不問，大怒，事下有司。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu because the erudits did not answer what was asked, answered what was not asked, was greatly angry; the matter was sent down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was furious that the erudits had dodged the question put to them and rambled on other topics, and he referred the matter to the judicial offices.

sentences.zh: 尚書硃整、褚䂮等奏：「旉等侵官離局，迷罔朝廷，崇飾惡言，假託無諱，請收旉等八人付廷尉科罪。

translations.literal: Ministers Zhu Zheng, Chu Lü and others memorialized: “Bin and others encroached on offices and departed from their bureaus, confused and deceived the court, elevated and adorned evil words, falsely relied on lacking taboo; request to seize Bin and eight others and hand to the commandant of justice to sentence crimes.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zheng, Chu Lü, and other ministers charged that Yu Bin and his colleagues had overstepped their authority, misled the throne, and spoken seditiously without restraint, and asked that all eight be handed to the commandant of justice for trial.”

sentences.zh: 」旉父純詣廷尉自首：「旉以議草見示，愚淺聽之。

translations.literal: ” Bin’s father Chun went to the commandant of justice and confessed himself: “Bin showed me the deliberation draft; foolish and shallow, I listened.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun went to the commandant of justice and confessed, “My son showed me his draft; I was a fool to let it pass.”

sentences.zh: 」詔免純罪。

translations.literal: ” An edict pardoned Chun’s crime.
translations.idiomatic: An edict absolved Yu Chun.”

sentences.zh: 廷尉劉頌又奏旉等大不敬，棄市論，求平議。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Liu Song again memorialized that Bin and others were greatly irreverent, with judgment of execution in the market, requesting balanced deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Liu Song renewed the charge of grave disrespect against Yu Bin and asked for a consensus sentence of public execution.

sentences.zh: 尚書又奏請報聽廷尉行刑。

translations.literal: The ministers again memorialized requesting reply to hear the commandant carry out execution.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry memorialized again for permission to carry out the sentence.

sentences.zh: 尚書夏侯駿謂硃整曰：「國家乃欲誅諫臣！

translations.literal: Minister Xiahou Jun said to Zhu Zheng, “The state then wishes to execute remonstrating ministers!”
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xiahou Jun told Zhu Zheng, “The court means to execute men for remonstrating!”

sentences.zh: 官立八座，正為此時，卿可共駁正之。

translations.literal: The office established eight seats; it is exactly for this moment; you can together refute and correct it.”
translations.idiomatic: The eight chief ministers exist for moments like this—you must join me in blocking this.”

sentences.zh: 」整不從，駿怒起，曰：「非所望也！

translations.literal: ” Zheng would not comply; Jun angrily rose and said, “This is not what was hoped!”
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zheng refused. Xiahou Jun rose in anger and cried, “Then I expected too much of you!”

sentences.zh: 」乃獨為駁議。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon alone he made a refuting deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore drafted a sole dissenting opinion.”

sentences.zh: 左僕射魏舒、右僕射下邳王晃等從駿議。

translations.literal: Left Supervisor Wei Shu, Right Supervisor Prince of Xiapi Huang and others followed Jun’s deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Left Supervisor Wei Shu, Right Supervisor Sima Huang of Xiapi, and others sided with Xiahou Jun.

sentences.zh: 奏留中七日，乃詔曰：「旉等備為儒官，不念奉憲制，不指答所問，敢肆其誣罔之言，以幹亂視聽。

translations.literal: The memorial was detained in the center seven days; then an edict said: “Bin and others fully are Confucian officials; they did not think on obeying statutes; they did not pointedly answer what was asked; they dared unleash their deceiving words, in order to disturb seeing and hearing.”
translations.idiomatic: The memorial sat seven days before an edict declared: “Yu Bin and the others hold scholarly rank yet ignored statute, evaded the question they were asked, and spread falsehoods to confuse the court.”

sentences.zh: 而旉是議主，應為戮首。

translations.literal: Yet Bin was the deliberation’s master; he ought to be chief of execution.
translations.idiomatic: As chief author Yu Bin should bear the heaviest penalty.”

sentences.zh: 但旉及家人並自首，大信不可奪。

translations.literal: But Bin and family members together confessed themselves; great trust cannot be taken away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu Bin and his kin had confessed, and the throne’s promise of mercy must stand.”

sentences.zh: 秦秀、傅珍前者虛妄，幸而得免，復不以為懼，當加罪戮，以彰凶慝。

translations.literal: Qin Xiu and Fu Zhen earlier were empty and false, luckily obtained pardon, again did not take it as fear; they should receive punishment and execution, in order to display vicious evil.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu and Fu Zhen had once escaped on false pretences; because they still showed no fear, they should be punished to expose their malice.”

sentences.zh: 猶復不忍，皆丐其死命。

translations.literal: Still again not bearing it, all begged their lives of death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor could not bear to kill them and commuted the sentences.”

sentences.zh: 秀、珍、旉等並除名。

translations.literal: Xiu, Zhen, Bin and others together were stripped of name.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu, Fu Zhen, Yu Bin, and the rest were dismissed from office and stripped of rank.”

sentences.zh: 」後數歲，復起為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: ” After several years, he was again raised to be Cavalier Gentleman-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later Yu Bin was recalled as Cavalier Gentleman-in-attendance.”

sentences.zh: 終於國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the end he was Libationer of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Libationer of the National University.

sentences.zh: 秦秀

translations.literal: Qin Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu

sentences.zh: 秦秀，字玄良，新興雲中人也。

translations.literal: Qin Xiu, courtesy name Xuanliang, was a man of Yunzhong in Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu, style Xuanliang, came from Yunzhong in Xinxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 父朗，魏驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Lang was Wei General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qin Lang had been Wei’s General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 秀少敦學行，以忠直知名。

translations.literal: Xiu in youth was earnest in learning and conduct, was known for loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was diligent in study and conduct and won a name for blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 咸甯中，為博士。

translations.literal: In the Xianning era, he was an erudit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianning era he served as an erudit.

sentences.zh: 何曾卒，下禮官議諡。

translations.literal: He Zeng died; it was sent down to ritual officials to deliberate posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When He Zeng died, the court asked ritual officials to propose a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 秀議曰：

translations.literal: Xiu deliberated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu argued:

sentences.zh: 故太宰何曾，雖階世族之胤，而少以高亮嚴肅，顯登王朝。

translations.literal: The late Grand Preceptor He Zeng, although he stepped from a noble clan’s descendant, yet in youth by high brightness and stern dignity, illustriously ascended the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Preceptor He Zeng, though born to a great house, first rose on brilliance and austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 事親有色養之名，在官奏科尹模，此二者實得臣子事上之概。

translations.literal: Serving kin he had the name of joyful support; in office he submitted regulations patterned on Yin Mo; these two things truly grasped the outline of ministers’ and sons’ serving superiors.
translations.idiomatic: He was praised for cheering his parents with dutiful care, and in office he drafted disciplinary statutes on the model of Yin Mo—both marks of how a subject should serve his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 然資性驕奢，不循軌則。

translations.literal: Yet his endowed nature was arrogant and extravagant; he did not follow tracks and rules.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his temperament ran to arrogance and excess, heedless of proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「節彼南山，惟石岩岩，赫赫師尹，人具爾瞻。

translations.literal: The Odes says, “Trim those southern mountains, only the rocks precipitous; awesomely the master Yin, the people all look to you.”
translations.idiomatic: The *Classic of Poetry* says of the minister Yin, “Lofty as the southern hills, awe-inspiring as their cliffs—all eyes are fixed on you.”

sentences.zh: 」言其德行高峻，動必以禮耳。

translations.literal: ” It speaks of his virtue and conduct being high and steep; in movement he must use ritual, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: That is praise for towering virtue and measured conduct.”

sentences.zh: 丘明有言：「儉，德之恭；

translations.literal: Qiu Ming had words: “Frugality is virtue’s reverence;
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Qiuming wrote, “Frugality is the crown of virtue;

sentences.zh: 侈，惡之大也。

translations.literal: extravagance is evil’s greatness.”
translations.idiomatic: extravagance is the chief of vices.”

sentences.zh: 」大晉受命，勞廉隱約，曾受寵二代，顯赫累世。

translations.literal: ” Great Jin received the mandate, toilsome integrity and hidden restraint; Zeng received favor through two generations, illustrious for piled generations.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin was founded on frugal service, yet He Zeng enjoyed imperial favor under two reigns and dazzled the realm for generations.

sentences.zh: 暨乎耳順之年，身兼三公之位，食大國之租，荷保傅之貴，執司徒之均。

translations.literal: Reaching the years of ear-harmony, his person concurrently held the three dukes’ positions, ate a great state’s rent, bore tutor and guardian’s honor, grasped the Minister of Education’s balance.
translations.idiomatic: Past his sixtieth year he held three grand offices at once, drew income from a great march, carried the titles of tutor to the heir, and controlled the Ministry of Education’s scales of justice.

sentences.zh: 二子皆金貂卿校，列於帝側。
